conviction_note: Four independent primary-document findings all lean the same way into a print where the only sell-side anchor is a single -$0.08 estimate; the dominant one is a one-time IEEPA tariff refund whose CBP disbursement window (Phase I opened 2026-04-20, 45-90 days to cash) lands inside VRA's quarter ended 2026-08-01 and which VRA's own stated policy books into income on receipt, sized against the $4.2m of tariff the CFO said was sitting in year-end inventory; I hold the number well inside the 20.6% implied move and the 10.4% median historical reaction because the probability the cash actually cleared before 1 August is nearer a coin flip than a certainty.

findings.finding: Vera Bradley's Q1 10-Q states it has filed IEEPA tariff refund claims and will 'recognize any related refunds and interest when cash is received' — and CBP's own refund machinery (CAPE Phase I opened 2026-04-20, disbursement target 45 days post-validation, 60-90 days from acceptance) puts that cash squarely inside the quarter being reported tomorrow, which ended 2026-08-01.
findings.why_not_priced: There is exactly one published estimate on this name (-$0.08) and the company's own filing says the timing of claim acceptance and payment 'remains uncertain', so no analyst can carry the refund in a model — it can only appear as an unforecastable one-time gain. The magnitude anchor is management's own: the CFO said on the 2026-03-12 call that 'Tariffs increased year-end inventory value by approximately $4.2 million' against a $76m inventory balance, so the annual incremental-duty run-rate flowing through COGS is a multiple of that and a refund plus statutory interest of a few million dollars is ~$0.10-0.18 per share on 28.4m shares — enough to flip a guided loss quarter to reported profit, and ~25-40% of the company's $12.5m cash balance. If this were priced you would see the stock bid into the event rather than -11.64% over five sessions, you would see a preview note naming a one-time refund line (there is none — no wire item on VRA since the 2026-09-01 date announcement), and a $89m-cap name would not be carrying a single estimate.
findings.independence: Different source, and not a company document: Bradley LLP's dated alert confirms CBP's CAPE system opened for Phase I refunds on 2026-04-20 with a 45-day disbursement target — https://www.bradley.com/insights/publications/2026/04/ieepa-update-phase-i-refunds-available-now — and CBP's own page states refunds are 'generally issued within 60 - 90 days following acceptance of the CAPE Declaration' — https://www.cbp.gov/trade/programs-administration/trade-remedies/ieepa-duty-refunds. The $4.2m inventory-tariff anchor is a third, separate source (the Q4 FY26 call transcript, https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/03/12/vera-bradley-vra-q4-2026-earnings-transcript/, 2026-03-12).

findings.finding: The Nordstrom wholesale capsule — announced 2026-06-16 with an 'initial run planned through the end of August' — is still live on nordstrom.com today with 12 Vera Bradley SKUs at full price ($30-$155), none marked down, while Nordstrom runs an 'up to 50% off summer styles' end-of-season clearance around it.
findings.why_not_priced: The announced end date has passed and no press release exists saying the relationship was extended, so nothing in the wire records it; the only way to know is to open the partner's own site. It is also a direct read on sell-through — a capsule that failed would be sitting in Nordstrom's clearance event alongside the rest of summer, and it is not. The Indirect segment ran $10.3m in the year-ago Q2 (down 52.5%) and $10.8m in Q1 (up 26.6%); an 89-door full-price program shipping through the quarter argues the Indirect line beats that run-rate, and a single-estimate consensus has no mechanism to reflect it. If this were priced there would be an extension press release or a note referencing expanded door count.
findings.independence: The June launch and door count are confirmed independently by the company's Q1 call ('On June 1st, we launched a focused back-to-school Vera Bradley capsule collection in 89 Nordstrom doors', https://www.theglobeandmail.com/investing/markets/markets-news/motley/2429875/vera-bradley-vra-q1-2027-earnings-transcript/, 2026-06-11) and by the launch release https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/06/16/3312498/0/en/vera-bradley-debuts-at-nordstrom-stores-nationwide-and-nordstrom-com.html (2026-06-16), which is where the 'through the end of August' window comes from. The live-page observation is the only evidence that it continued.

findings.finding: The cancelled Annual Outlet Sale, announced 2026-03-12 as a headline negative, falls almost entirely in fiscal Q1, not Q2 — the 2025 sale ran 30 April to 4 May 2025 and VRA's Q1 FY26 ended 3 May 2025, so only one of its five days sat in the year-ago Q2 comparison base.
findings.why_not_priced: It requires joining the sale's calendar dates to a 52/53-week retail fiscal calendar, which no aggregator does and no coverage exists to do. The default reading — and the one the March cancellation headline invites — is that a dropped multi-million-dollar liquidation event is a drag on the quarters ahead. It is not: VRA already lapped it in Q1 FY27 and still grew consolidated revenue 7.8%, so the Q2 comparison is effectively clean and the liquidation revenue that did go is gross-margin dilutive anyway. If this were priced, the March cancellation would not still be the framing device in the local and trade coverage.
findings.independence: The fiscal period end date of 3 May 2025 is from a different document, the Q1 FY27 10-Q's comparative column — https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1495320/000162828026042444/vra-20260502.htm (2026-06-11). Note this shares no document with finding 1 beyond that period-end date; the substance is from the 2025 sale announcement.

findings.finding: Vera Bradley's own DTC homepage today carries no sitewide percentage discount at all — free shipping over $99, new fall arrivals, personalization, and a Harry Potter 'Sorcerer's Stone' collection that has no press release and no trade coverage anywhere.
findings.why_not_priced: Nobody reads a nano-cap's homepage into a print. It is a forward read rather than a Q2 read, and it is the weakest item here, but it is the cheapest available check on whether the 430bp of Q1 gross-margin expansion management attributed to 'disciplined promotional strategies' survived into the back half — a brand that had lost pricing power would be leading with a percentage-off banner in mid-September. If the market had focused on it there would be a note on promotional cadence; VRA has one estimate and no notes.
findings.independence: Weakly corroborated by the same live-page evidence base as finding 2 (Vera Bradley product sitting at full price on Nordstrom while Nordstrom clears summer). Treat findings 2 and 4 as one full-price-posture cluster, not two independent reads.

searched_and_found_nothing: Cause of the -11.64% five-session slide into the print: no 8-K, no press release, no news item, no analyst action and no filing of any kind since the 2026-07-24 executive severance 8-K. I could not explain the move and am not treating it as information.

13D/13G activity: Fund 1 Investments (Jonathan Lennon) holds ~10% on a 13D last amended 2025-11-20, and the only 2026 item is a Nomura passive 13G/A at 2.6% (2026-02-17). No new activist filing, no take-private approach, nothing in the last seven months.

Insider Form 4s: nothing filed since 2026-07-07, and that was a tax-withholding disposition by CEO Ian Bickley, not a sale. Director Andrew Meslow's 24,926-share open-market buy at $3.73 is 2026-06-12 — three months stale and immediately post-print, so not information about this quarter.

Store count: the 10-Q gives 112 stores at 2026-05-02 (26 full-line, 86 outlet) against 126 a year earlier, and management flagged four new outlets to open, but verabradley.com's store locator exposes no enumerable total and I could not get an independent current count to test the closure pace.
Balance-sheet stress: zero drawn on the $75m ABL with $68.0m availability to May 2028, no going-concern language, no covenant trip. There is no distress angle here.
Buyback: $30.0m authorised through December 2027 with zero executed to date — no share-count surprise available on the Q2 cover page.
Pura Vida: divested 2025-03-31, only a $1.8m contingent earn-out receivable remains. No further impairment set-up to find.

Short interest: could not retrieve any 2026 settlement-date figure; Nasdaq and the aggregators would not serve. The baseline's 47:1 put/call open-interest ratio sits on only 2,412 total contracts (~240k shares notional) and is too small to read as positioning.

A dollar quantification of VRA's own IEEPA refund claim: neither the 10-K, the 10-Q, nor either call transcript names a figure. My size on finding 1 is inferred from the $4.2m of tariff in year-end inventory and the CFO's '19% to 15%' rate commentary, not from a disclosed claim amount.
Urban Outfitters collaboration — chased and dropped: the collection is dated 2024-08-27 in the URL path and is not a 2026 event.
baseline_tension: It cuts against the tape: the stock is -11.64% over five sessions and -9.48% over twenty into the print with put open interest 47x calls, while everything I found — a refundable tariff claim whose CBP payment window sits inside the quarter, a wholesale program still selling at full price past its announced end date, and a feared outlet-sale hole that was actually a Q1 event already lapped — argues the quarter is better than a single stale -$0.08 estimate implies; the baseline's null 25-delta skew means the market is making no explicit directional statement here to disagree with.
